content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently overestimate prices in the short term, especially after bullish sentiment spikes.", "Sentiment shifts toward bearishness after auction events, causing forecasted prices to lag behind true market outcomes.", "Model forecasts exhibit mean-reversion bias when official event net supply is negative, underestimating volatility.", "High bullish sentiment correlates with forecast overshoots, but fails to predict sharp downward corrections post-auction.", "Forecast accuracy deteriorates when sentiment is mixed or negative, particularly after consecutive auction events.", "Model bias toward upward trends persists despite negative supply net, indicating insufficient adjustment to policy-driven supply shocks.", "Sentiment and forecast divergence is most pronounced during periods of high event frequency and negative supply net.", "Forecast models should incorporate sentiment decay rates and event lag effects to reduce persistent overestimation."]}
